Maven module scaffolding for the Keycloak MCP SPI. Keycloak BOM 26.6.0, Java 21, provided-scope Keycloak deps, test deps (JUnit 5, Mockito, Testcontainers 1.20.4, testcontainers-keycloak 3.5.1, RestAssured), Surefire + Failsafe + Jacoco. mvn dependency:resolve green. META-INF service files seeded with comment placeholders; classes register as slices 2-4 land. .gitignore tightened to **/target/.

Slice 1 JWT primitives. 8 production classes + 8 test classes; 49 unit tests pass; jacoco 97% instructions / 88% branches across jwt/config/util packages. HS256 sign via Keycloak JWSBuilder; verify via HMACProvider. Per-realm key caching. snake_case wire format. Open: Keycloak deprecation warning in JWSBuilder.type(); revisit Slice 6.

Slice 2 scope override mapper. McpScopeOverrideMapper extends AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper, implements OIDCAccessTokenMapper. Reads userSession.getNote('knobby_scopes') and replaces AccessToken.scope. 10 tests, 59/59 cumulative. Deviated from spec by omitting OIDCIDTokenMapper/UserInfoTokenMapper interfaces because IDToken has no setScope; documented in javadoc. Mapper class = factory (Keycloak OIDC conflates them via AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.create() returning this). Registered in META-INF/services/org.keycloak.protocol.ProtocolMapper.

Slice 3 Authenticator (suspend). Authenticator reads per-realm knobby.web.host from AuthenticatorConfig, builds PickerRequestToken (carries kc_client_id, kc_tab_id, auth_session_id for resume), signs with per-realm HMAC, 302 via context.challenge(Response.seeOther()). Factory exposes knobby.web.host as configurable property; init() instantiates singleton signer and logs realms with HMAC keys. 27 new tests, 86/86 cumulative. Side fix: oauth_state relaxed from required to optional in both token builders (OAuth 2.1 client may omit state).

Slice 4 ResourceProvider (resume). JAX-RS endpoint at /realms/{realm}/mcp-picker-callback validates picker-result JWT, finds auth session via AuthenticationSessionManager (cookie + jti fallback), writes knobby_tenant_id/knobby_scopes session notes, 302s to AuthenticationFlowURLHelper.getLastExecutionUrl(authSession). Function injection of session-manager factory + resume-URL builder enables happy-path unit testing. 22 new tests, 108/108 cumulative. Added kc_client_id, kc_tab_id, auth_session_id to PickerResultToken so callback finds session from HMAC-signed payload (not query params). Fixed Slice 1 tamper-test bug (flipping last base64url char of 256-bit sig can land on unused bits).

Slice 5 minimal Testcontainers IT (McpSpiLoadingIT). Builds JAR via mvn package, runs Keycloak 26.6.0 testcontainer with JAR mounted via withProviderLibsFrom, asserts GET /realms/master/mcp-picker-callback returns 400 missing_token (proving SPI registers and handler runs). 39 s runtime. 108 unit + 1 IT all green. Full OAuth-flow IT (browser cookies + Knobby-web mock + realm import + test-realm.json) deliberately deferred; production smoke tests cover those paths.

Slice 6 build pipeline + deployment config. build.sh rewritten: reads SPI version from pom.xml, runs mvn package -DskipITs, stages JAR to /target/providers/, passes all build-args to docker. test.sh created (mvn verify in src/providers). Dockerfile env-var comments updated to per-realm. cloudrun.yaml gets commented per-realm HMAC stanza + fix for pre-existing KC_BOOTSTRAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD= typo (trailing = made env name invalid). HandoffTokenSigner rewritten to use modern MacSignatureSignerContext + KeyWrapper API, eliminating deprecation warnings (ADR-008). End-to-end: ./test.sh green (108+1, 46s); ./build.sh produces keycloak:local image with SPI JAR baked in and OCI labels stamped.

Created the four remaining shell scripts AGENTS.md lists as expected (clean.sh, run.sh, deploy.sh, prune.sh). Modeled on ~/work/knobby/apps/ patterns. clean.sh removes /target/, src/providers/target/, build.json, and reports/. run.sh starts a postgres sidecar + the locally-built keycloak image on port 10000 with admin/admin, --clean flag for full teardown. deploy.sh chains build.sh + push.sh + gcloud run deploy --image (preserving cloudrun.yaml env bindings), then tails logs. prune.sh deletes inactive Cloud Run revisions AND Artifact Registry image versions older than the last N (default 5), preserving any image still referenced by ANY revision. All four bash -n clean; clean.sh tested live.

Updated build.sh to use sortable unique version tag YYYYMMDDhhmmss-<commit> (UTC) instead of the prior Keycloak-version-prefixed tag. Each build now applies three tags in one docker build: keycloak:local (run.sh + local inspect), <registry>:<timestamp>-<commit> (versioned; pushed; what Cloud Run revisions pin to), and <registry>:latest (moving tag for convenience pulls). build.json now records build_timestamp and latest_tag in addition to remote_tag. push.sh updated to push both versioned and latest tags. Verified end-to-end: docker build successfully tagged 3 ways.

Silenced three categories of cosmetic noise from mvn test/verify output: (1) Keycloak's JBossLoggerFinder 'LogManager accessed before the property was set' ERROR — fixed by setting -Djava.util.logging.manager=org.jboss.logmanager.LogManager in Surefire/Failsafe argLine. Required adding maven-dependency-plugin properties execution to resolve the JAR's filesystem path into ${net.bytebuddy:byte-buddy-agent:jar}. (3) JVM CDS sharing warning — fixed by adding -Xshare:off. Log output now uses proper JBoss format with ISO timestamps. The remaining ERROR/WARN lines in test output are SPI's own logs from test cases deliberately exercising error paths (user_mismatch, REPLAY, BAD_SIGNATURE, MISSING_HMAC_KEY, etc.) — these are expected and prove the logging code is correctly wired. 108 unit + 1 IT all green; verify total time 47s.

First Cloud Run deploy of the SPI image (20260610050525-b0a2d5e) coincided with Hibernate 42P01 'relation does not exist' errors (offline_user_session on session-persist commit, realm from the user-session-purge-expired task) against the Neon Postgres pooler. Debugged by running the EXACT failed image ID locally under the production entrypoint (start --optimized) against a Postgres 16 sidecar whose schema was pre-initialised by the vanilla image: clean startup, admin logins, realm create/list, 4 rows written to offline_user_session, mcp-picker-callback serving, 6+ hour soak with zero errors. kc.sh show-config diff vanilla-vs-SPI: one line (provider JAR registration). Verdict: environmental transient on the Neon pooler/compute side — failures clustered by time window (a known-good rollback image also failed in the window), and stock-Keycloak SQL failed on tables that exist while other connections in the same process saw them. Reverted the speculative JAX-RS edits (final removal, @Path('/') removal) made under the disproved route-table theory. Added check_image.sh forensics script, gitignored build.json (volatile build output), recorded TD-007 (pin base image by SHA digest), TD-008 (run.sh start-dev cannot reproduce optimized-image issues), resolved TD-003 (bootstrap admin login verified on fixed binding). Operator redeployed the SPI image successfully after the window cleared.

Implemented spec §5.1 step-0 short-circuit guard in McpTenantPickerAuthenticator.authenticate(). When the client is not an MCP client (lacks the mcp-default client scope as default or optional, checked via ClientModel.getClientScopes(true/false).containsKey), the authenticator calls context.success() and returns, letting regular web logins and non-MCP clients pass through untouched. This lets browser-mcp-tenant-pick be bound realm-wide without hijacking normal logins; mcp-default is now the on/off switch for the whole handoff. Added MCP_CLIENT_SCOPE constant + isMcpClient(ClientModel) helper. Verified ClientModel.getClientScopes(boolean)->Map<String,ClientScopeModel> and AbstractAuthenticationFlowContext.success() against the 26.6.0 JARs. TDD: 5 new unit tests (non-MCP short-circuits with success / never challenges / never fails; optional-scope MCP proceeds; default-scope does not short-circuit); updated setUp to make the happy-path client an MCP client. 113 unit + 1 IT green. ADR-009 recorded.

Installed Gitleaks 8.30.1 and TruffleHog 3.95.8 under /tmp/security-tools and ran local secret scans. Built McpClientRegistrationPolicy + factory (ERRATA-001, SPI design 5.8) to close the MCP DCR bootstrapping circular dependency. afterRegister marks every anonymous-DCR client atomically inside the registration transaction: sets knobby.mcp=true attribute, assigns default (mcp-default + author bundle) and optional (knobby:admin) client scopes, binds browser-mcp-tenant-pick via setAuthenticationFlowBindingOverride; missing scope/flow throws ClientRegistrationPolicyException (rolls back). Scope lists + flow alias are ComponentModel config props (config-driven decision) with settled defaults as fallback. Deployed as anonymous CRP. Updated McpTenantPickerAuthenticator.isMcpClient to PREFER the knobby.mcp attribute over mcp-default scope, and reworded the 5.1 short-circuit as a pure safety net (activates ADR-010/TD-009 escape hatch). Verified all 26.6.0 model-API signatures (ClientRegistrationPolicy(Factory), ClientModel.addClientScope/setAuthenticationFlowBindingOverride, RealmModel.getFlowByAlias, KeycloakModelUtils.getClientScopeByName, AbstractClientRegistrationPolicyFactory, ProviderConfigurationBuilder) against the pinned BOM jars via javap before coding; confirmed ClientRegistrationPolicyException extends RuntimeException so afterRegister can throw to roll back. B1 (AllowedGrantTypes) deferred; beforeRegister left as no-op stub. TDD: 15 new unit tests + 1 real-DCR testcontainers IT (drops the default Trusted Hosts anon policy, registers the CRP, does anonymous DCR, asserts client shape). 129 unit + 2 IT green. ADR-011 recorded. No app/mcp-consent changes this pass; web spec 7.5 got an interim pointer note only.

Diagnosed the production client=null 400 on the mcp-picker-callback final hop as a contract desync (ERRATA-003), not a resume-mechanics bug. The SPI callback recovers the suspended session+client from kc_client_id/kc_tab_id/auth_session_id claims echoed in the signed picker-result, but web spec 2.2/3.3 never told the app to echo them, so the app omitted them and getClientByClientId(null) returned null. Fix A (chosen over re-architecting around getActionUrl/session_code): app echoes the three kc_* claims from the SERVER-HELD picker-request (not the client POST body, to avoid a session-fixation surface). SPI-side: added a missing_correlation guard before the client lookup (distinct from client_not_found) with a spec-pointing WARN + isBlank helper + marker note; 1 new unit test signs the app real claim set (no kc_*) and asserts missing_correlation (18 provider tests, all suites green). Docs: ERRATA-003; reconciled stale SPI design 5.3 (had jti-correlation + AuthenticationProcessor.continueAuthentication, neither shipped) to the real AuthenticationSessionManager + getLastExecutionUrl design; web spec 2.2 step 5 + 3.3 add the three required echoed claims with the server-side-sourcing security note; ADR-012. Confirmed ERRATA-002 (app-side /mcp/consent split) does NOT cover this. App-side echo in KnobbyApi (separate repo) is the remaining change that clears the 400.

Fixed the /mcp/consent <-> Keycloak infinite redirect loop (ERRATA-004), exposed once the ERRATA-003 correlation echo let mcp-picker-callback resume the flow instead of 400-ing. Root cause from the HAR: callback resumes via getLastExecutionUrl, which makes Keycloak re-invoke the tenant-picker authenticator's authenticate() (a CHALLENGED execution resumes through authenticate(), NOT action(), because it rides a redirect not a form POST), and authenticate() was not re-entrant so it re-issued a fresh picker-request every time -> 303 back to /mcp/consent forever. Fix: McpTenantPickerAuthenticator.authenticate() opens with a resume guard reading a new auth note knobby.mcp.picker.completed (written by McpPickerCallbackResourceProvider.writeSessionNotes alongside the tenant/scope user-session notes) -> context.success() and finish. Explicit marker rather than tenant-note presence because the validator's Jackson readJsonContent bypasses the builder's requireString, so a signed-but-malformed null-tenant result could still loop. Shared public constant AUTH_NOTE_PICKER_COMPLETED prevents writer/reader drift. NO app-side change (loop was evidence ERRATA-003 works). Also hardened smoke-mcp.sh to reclaim a stale loopback listener (Errno 98 Address already in use from a prior aborted run) and added diag-mcp-flow.sh (read-only) to dump realm default browser flow + browser-mcp-tenant-pick execution requirements. Earlier in the session confirmed via Cookie-path vs broker-path experiment that the picker fires on Cookie login but the per-client browser-flow override is lost after the Google broker round-trip (separate finding, not yet fixed). TDD: 3 new unit tests (authenticator finishes-without-challenge / still-challenges-without-note; callback sets marker); 133 unit + 2 IT green. ERRATA-004, ADR-013.

Fixed two McpClientRegistrationPolicy client-shape defects exposed once ERRATA-004 let smoke-mcp.sh run end-to-end (ERRATA-006). Defect 1: mcp-default + author bundle missing from the DCR'd client's DEFAULT client scopes though effective (aud correct). Root cause: Keycloak's OIDC DCR pre-binds the request `scope` field values as OPTIONAL client scopes BEFORE the CRP afterRegister runs, and ClientModel.addClientScope is a no-op when a binding already exists, so it never promotes optional->default; knobby:admin (not requested) was placed correctly, the tell. Fix: assignScopes now removeClientScope then addClientScope(scope, asDefault) so placement is authoritative. Defect 2: Keycloak built-in OAUTH_GRANT consent double-upped the knobby /mcp/consent wizard because the mcp-hardening consent-required executor sets consentRequired=true. Fix: CRP setConsentRequired(false); safe because client-policy executors fire on triggerOnEvent BEFORE the CRP's triggerAfterRegister (verified against 26.6.0 AbstractClientRegistrationProvider bytecode, offset 228<237), so the CRP wins. Verified removeClientScope + setConsentRequired present in 26.6.0 via javap. The IT previously sent NO scope field (why it passed while prod failed); now sends scope (reproducing prod), clears ALL default registration policies so the scoped anonymous DCR reaches the CRP (Allowed Client Scopes policy was 403-ing the scoped DCR), and asserts default-scope placement + consentRequired=false. TDD: 2 new unit tests (promotion removes-before-adds; consent suppressed) + tightened no-op test; 135 unit + 2 IT green. ERRATA-006, ADR-014. Still open: TD-010 (broker-path per-client browser-flow override lost after IdP round-trip).

Ran the ERRATA-005 SDK spike (Keycloak 26.6.0) to settle the fresh-session/brokered-login tenant-picker gap: fresh cookieless MCP logins never reached /mcp/consent because Keycloak skips browser-flow executions placed after an IdP-redirect step for brokered logins (issue #10250). Decompiled LoginActionsService, AuthenticationProcessor, AuthenticationFlowURLHelper, IdentityBrokerService and resolved all 5 open questions. Conclusion: host the SAME McpTenantPickerAuthenticator in a per-IdP Post Broker Login Flow; it works UNMODIFIED there. Key findings: (1) brokered login keeps ONE AuthenticationSessionModel keyed by (rootAuthSessionId, client, tabId) - postBrokerLoginGet/Post recover it by clientId+tabId - so authSession.getClient() is the original MCP client, context.getUser() is the brokered user, and the ERRATA-004 re-entrancy note lives on that same session (loop does NOT reappear on IdP path); (2) isMcpClient guard is resolvable AND load-bearing there (per-IdP flow shared with web logins, no-ops non-MCP clients); (3) suspend/resume works because AuthenticationFlowURLHelper.getLastExecutionUrl is flow-path-agnostic - rebuilds from current.flow.path auth note, which LoginActionsService.brokerLoginFlow sets to post-broker-login via AuthenticationProcessor.setFlowPath - so the callback's existing getLastExecutionUrl redirect resumes the post-broker flow correctly; (4) one shared post-broker flow reusable across Google+Microsoft; (5) runs after first-broker-login, no conflict. FIX IS CONFIG-ONLY: no change to McpTenantPickerAuthenticator logic or McpPickerCallbackResourceProvider, and NO app-side change (picker-request/result contract + correlation claims + fixed /mcp-picker-callback URL identical regardless of hosting flow). Code touch was doc-only: §5.1 guard reclassified safety-net(browser)/load-bearing(post-broker) in comment + factory HELP_TEXT + marker note both flows; each post-broker picker execution needs its own knobby.web.host AuthenticatorConfig (per-execution). Docs: ERRATA-005 spike write-up + status flip, SPI §5.1, setup guide new D.2a (create post-broker-mcp-tenant-pick + bind per-IdP), ADR-015, CHANGELOG, status, concepts, insights. Operator action: apply config per env; acceptance test MUST be cookieless. Rejected alternative: RequiredActionProvider (one hook both paths) - would require changing the callback resume mechanism, larger/riskier. 135 unit + 2 IT green (doc-only code touch). TD-010 now resolved-by-ERRATA-005.

Root-caused the fresh-session /mcp/consent dead-end (ERRATA-007) using chrome.har + Keycloak idp.log + app.log. Keycloak/SPI side confirmed fully working end-to-end: DCR marks client (consent-suppressed log line present, so ERRATA-006 code deployed), post-broker tenant picker fires on the fresh/brokered path (Emitting MCP picker request under login-actions/post-broker-login, so ERRATA-005 config works), redirects browser to prod.knobby.io/mcp/consent?token=<picker-request JWT>. The picker-request token is valid, HMAC-signed, aud=knobby-web-mcp-consent, TTL 300s, and carries the user (sub=knobby_sub). BUG is entirely app-side (KnobbyApi): the /mcp/consent wizard gates on a knobby.io app session (GET /api/v1/auth/me) instead of trusting the signed token. For a user not logged into the app this triggers the app's own OIDC login (client knobby-prod-web); because the MCP flow is SUSPENDED at the picker, Keycloak has not created an SSO session yet, so the app's prompt=none fails and falls back to a second interactive Google login; that login then LOSES the return_url=/mcp/consent?token=... and lands on prod.knobby.io/ (home). HAR proof: /mcp/consent requested exactly once, mcp-picker-callback hit 0 times -> MCP flow never resumes, loopback /callback never fires, test hangs. Also saw REFRESH_TOKEN_ERROR invalid_grant 'Token is not active' on a stale app session, which breaks even the warm path. FIX (app-side): /mcp/consent must authenticate from the signed ?token= handoff (validate HMAC + iss + aud + exp + jti single-use), render the wizard for token.sub, and NOT require an app session or login redirect; on submit sign picker-result and POST to mcp-picker-callback (unchanged). ERRATA-007 documents BOTH flows the fix must make correct: (1) user already logged in (warm; currently fragile - a failed app-session refresh breaks it), (2) user not logged in (cold; currently fully broken). Wrote ERRATA-007 hand-off for the app team. No Keycloak/SPI code change. Separate open Keycloak item: Issue 1 (consent-required executor re-applies consentRequired=true on post-register update, ERRATA-006 - drop the executor from mcp-hardening), unverified because the flow dead-ended before reaching it. User's separate architectural musing (app dropping its own login.html to always use Keycloak's hosted login, per keycloak-theming-guide.md) noted as orthogonal to this bug and parked.

Added smoke-mcp.sh assertions for consentRequired=false and directAccessGrantsEnabled=false. The consentRequired assertion confirmed in production that ERRATA-006/ADR-014's claim was WRONG: the CRP's setConsentRequired(false) does NOT win over the mcp-hardening consent-required executor (its autoConfigure mutates the client representation, applied to the model AFTER the CRP's afterRegister, re-setting consentRequired=true; the ConsentRequiredClientRegistrationPolicy if present also forces it). Result: Keycloak's built-in Grant Access screen still double-ups the knobby /mcp/consent wizard. The IT was green only because it strips all registration policies (no consent-forcer runs there). Corrected to a CONFIG fix: remove the consent-required executor from mcp-hardening AND the consent-required CRP if present. Established (answering the user's security question) that dropping Keycloak consent does NOT weaken enforcement: the tenant picker + /mcp/consent wizard are gated by the auth flow - picker is REQUIRED in both browser-mcp-tenant-pick and post-broker-mcp-tenant-pick, it suspends via context.challenge, and Keycloak issues no token until the app POSTs a valid HMAC-signed, jti-single-use, correlation-bound picker-result to mcp-picker-callback (action() rejects bypass). That is stronger and non-redundant with Keycloak's generic consent. The one real bypass is a non-browser grant (Direct Access Grants / ROPC) which skips the browser flow entirely - so smoke-mcp.sh now asserts directAccessGrantsEnabled=false, and the deferred B1 (AllowedGrantTypes CRP, SPI design 5.8 beforeRegister stub) should enforce grant-type restriction atomically at registration. CRP retains setConsentRequired(false) as belt-and-suspenders with an honest comment (effective once the forcers are removed). Docs corrected: ERRATA-006 (CORRECTION callout + summary), setup guide D.5 CRP table + D.6 executor table + checklist, keycloak.prd.md System-1/System-2 tables, CRP code comment. ADR-016 supersedes the consent portion of ADR-014 (scope-promotion portion of ADR-014 stands). No SPI behavior change - comment + smoke assertions only. Bytecode facts: ConsentRequiredExecutor.executeOnEvent handles 2 ClientCRUDContext events (register + update), autoConfigure(rep) sets rep.consentRequired=true, update branch also calls beforeUpdate(getTargetClient(), rep) on the model.

Implemented B1 / AllowedGrantTypes (ADR-017, spec 13a.1), folded into McpClientRegistrationPolicy.beforeRegister + beforeUpdate rather than a separate provider (per the one-provider note in 5.8). rejectDisallowedGrants(ClientRepresentation) throws ClientRegistrationPolicyException (400 at DCR) if the proposed client enables any non-authorization-code grant: directAccessGrantsEnabled (password/ROPC), implicitFlowEnabled, serviceAccountsEnabled (client_credentials), the device authorization grant (attr oauth2.device.authorization.grant.enabled=true), or CIBA (attr oidc.ciba.grant.enabled=true). Null client is a safe no-op. Security invariant, deliberately NOT admin-tunable (a loosenable denylist is a footgun); runs on update too so a client can't widen its grants after registration. This closes the one real bypass of the flow-enforced tenant picker + /mcp/consent: they are gated by the browser auth flow, so a non-browser grant (ROPC issues tokens with no browser flow at all) would skip them - which matters now that Keycloak's built-in consent screen is dropped (ADR-016). Defense-in-depth over the disabled realm Direct Grant flow (setup guide D.10). API verified via javap against 26.6.4: ClientRegistrationContext.getClient() returns ClientRepresentation; isDirectAccessGrantsEnabled/isImplicitFlowEnabled/isServiceAccountsEnabled (Boolean, nullable) + getAttributes(). TDD: 7 new unit tests (each disallowed grant rejected on beforeRegister; beforeUpdate rejects directAccessGrants; authCodeOnly passes; nullClient safe) + 1 new real-DCR testcontainers IT (anonymousDcr_requestingPasswordGrant_isRejected asserts a grant_types [authorization_code, password] DCR returns 4xx). 142 unit + 3 IT green. Updated the stale beforeRegister_isNoOp unit test (it was a placeholder). Marker block + spec 13a.1 flipped from deferred to IMPLEMENTED; 5.8 note + pseudocode updated. Remaining open across the MCP work: ERRATA-007 (app-side /mcp/consent token-auth, KnobbyApi repo). Keycloak/SPI side now complete including grant-type hardening.

Synchronized handoff documentation after the committed B1/ADR-017 work. Marked B1 and the CRP bootstrap as shipped in the tech-debt register, updated ERRATA-001's current state, corrected ERRATA-006's status to distinguish scope-promotion code from consent-required config removal, and replaced the SPI design's stale standalone/deferred AllowedGrantTypesPolicy text with the implemented McpClientRegistrationPolicy.beforeRegister/beforeUpdate shape. Active blocker remains ERRATA-007 in KnobbyApi plus environment config removal of consent-required.

Next: Group B (RT-007 mcp-default doc contradiction + smoke guard, RT-012 admin-role reconcile) and Group C (cloudrun bootstrap removal incl username, dedicated SA instructions, digest pin). smoke.sh must be run by the user after redeploy (needs ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET + tests live server).

Group B of red-team remediation. RT-007: fixed contradictory mcp-default instructions - setup guide D.4 assigned type Default->None (must not be realm-default; CRP assigns per-client), E.2 checklist updated (CRP does scope+flow binding at registration, superseding Option A/B). Added smoke.sh Test 11 guard that fails if knobby-{env}-web carries mcp-default (default or optional) - would misroute web logins into MCP consent path. Primary MCP discriminator is the knobby.mcp attribute (ADR-011) but mcp-default is a fallback signal so keep it off the web client. Recommend splitting admin clients by duty. bash -n smoke.sh OK. User must run smoke.sh against the live server (needs ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET) to see the new RT-007 guard pass.
